name: dbolympics
source: imported from heron (commit 859f7c3, Apache-2.0: schema/LICENSE-heron, schema/NOTICE-heron)

modules.name: identity
modules.description:
tenants, users, RBAC, sessions, API creds, teams.
Foundation module: almost everything references tenants(id) and
users(id). Self-contained: tables + constraints + FK indexes +
selected comments. See CONVENTIONS.md and SCHEMA-MAP.md.

modules.name: geo
modules.description:
geography & i18n reference data + tenant addresses.
Mostly GLOBAL reference tables (not tenant-scoped); addresses are tenant-scoped.
Ends by wiring tenants' currency/locale defaults to geo (deferred FKs).

modules.name: catalog
modules.description:
products, variants, categories, brands, attributes, media.
The product master for the platform. Every table is tenant-scoped. Cross-schema
FKs target tenants(id) and users(id) only (product_reviews,
review_votes). Loads after 00-02. See CONVENTIONS.md and SCHEMA-MAP.md.
Soft-deletable entities (deleted_at): brands, products, product_variants,
categories, collections. Fact-ish/immutable junctions and the closure table
are not soft-deleted.

modules.name: pricing
modules.description:
price lists, prices, discounts, coupons, tax, promotions.
Money lives here: every monetary column is numeric(14,4) paired with a
currency_code char(3) -> currencies(code). Cross-schema FKs reach back to
identity (tenants), geo (currencies, countries, regions, postal_zones), and
catalog (product_variants, products). promotions are deliberately STANDALONE:
marketing (module 10) references promotions, never the reverse.
Soft-deletable: price_lists, discounts, coupons, promotions (deleted_at NULL = live).
See CONVENTIONS.md and SCHEMA-MAP.md.

modules.name: inventory
modules.description:
warehouses, stock locations, suppliers, on-hand stock,
the immutable movement ledger, reservations, purchase orders, lots/serials,
goods receipts and manual adjustments.
Cross-schema FKs (all backward-numbered, per SCHEMA-MAP):
  * tenant_id            -> tenants(id)        (every table is T)
  * created_by_user_id   -> users(id)          (actor on movements/adjustments)
  * addresses(id)    -> warehouse physical location
  * currencies(code) -> money on supplier_products / purchase_orders
  * product_variants(id) -> the unit of inventory everywhere
Forward reference NOT taken: stock_reservations conceptually holds stock
"against an order" (orders, module 06, higher-numbered). The contract
forbids forward FKs and SCHEMA-MAP does not expose sales keys to this module,
so order_id is carried as a plain bigint WITHOUT a FK constraint. See note
on that table.
Immutable tables (created_at only, no updated_at, no deleted_at):
  stock_movements (ledger). Everything else is a business table.
See CONVENTIONS.md and SCHEMA-MAP.md.

modules.name: sales
modules.description:
carts, orders, order items, fulfillments, shipments,
returns, gift cards. The CORE fact tables of the commerce domain.
References lower modules: tenants/users, addresses/currencies,
product_variants, discounts/coupons, warehouses.
Self-contained: tables + constraints + FK indexes + selected comments.
See CONVENTIONS.md and SCHEMA-MAP.md.
Immutability / soft-delete policy (per CONVENTIONS.md):
  * orders, order_items, order_status_history are immutable FACT rows and are
    NOT soft-deletable (no deleted_at). orders/order_items keep updated_at
    (status/totals are mutated in place); order_status_history is append-only
    (created_at only, no updated_at).
  * gift_card_transactions is an append-only ledger (created_at only).
  * No table in this module is soft-deletable.

modules.name: billing
modules.description:
payments, refunds, invoices, credit notes, payouts, the
double-entry ledger, plans/subscriptions/metered usage, dunning, wallets.
The money-heavy module: every monetary column is numeric(14,4) paired with a
currency_code char(3) -> currencies(code). Cross-schema FKs point only at
lower-or-equal-numbered modules: identity (01), geo (02), sales (06).
IMMUTABLE tables (created_at only, no updated_at/deleted_at):
  ledger_entries (append-only double-entry ledger).
Everything else is a business table with created_at/updated_at.
See CONVENTIONS.md and SCHEMA-MAP.md. Comments live mostly inline here
(≈70% coverage; some tables intentionally left undocumented).

modules.name: crm
modules.description:
B2B CRM: accounts, contacts, leads, pipelines, opportunities,
deals, activities, tasks, notes, contact lists.
IMPORTANT: accounts are the TENANT'S OWN customer companies (B2B). They
are tenant-scoped via tenant_id and are NOT tenants (the platform's
customer orgs). Sales reps are users (is_staff); the people the reps
sell to are contacts hanging off accounts.
Soft-deletable: accounts, contacts (deleted_at, NULL = live). Everything else
is hard-deleted / cascaded. opportunity_stages is an ordered LOOKUP table.
See CONVENTIONS.md and SCHEMA-MAP.md.

modules.name: support
modules.description:
tickets, messages, SLAs, agents, CSAT, knowledge base.
Customer-support domain. Cross-schema FKs only to identity (01): tenants(id)
for tenancy and users(id) for ticket requesters / agent records. All tables
are tenant-scoped. ticket_events is IMMUTABLE (created_at only, no updated_at
— it is an append-only audit of ticket changes). See CONVENTIONS.md and
SCHEMA-MAP.md.
Soft-deletable entities (deleted_at): knowledge_articles, macros.

modules.name: marketing
modules.description:
campaigns, segments, A/B tests, referrals, loyalty.
Tenant-scoped throughout. Backward (lower-numbered) FKs used: tenants,
users, currencies, orders (nullable conversion attribution),
promotions (optional campaign promo link). loyalty_transactions is an
IMMUTABLE earn/burn ledger (created_at only, no updated_at, no deleted_at).
See CONVENTIONS.md and SCHEMA-MAP.md.

modules.name: analytics
modules.description:
product analytics: the events fact table, web sessions,
page views, device profiles, feature usage, experiments (variants +
assignments), funnels (+ steps), cohorts (+ members), pre-aggregated daily
metrics, and KPI snapshots.
IMMUTABLE fact/log tables (events, page_views, feature_usage) carry only
created_at/occurred_at — no updated_at, no deleted_at. The remaining tables
are mutable definition/config tables with created_at/updated_at.
Cross-schema FK targets: tenants(id), users(id).
All other FKs are intra-analytics and reference lower-or-equal tables.
See CONVENTIONS.md and SCHEMA-MAP.md.

modules.name: comms
modules.description:
notifications, in-app messaging, webhooks, and outbound
email/sms/push delivery records. Loads after identity (01). Cross-schema FKs
target only tenants(id) and users(id). Self-contained:
tables + constraints + FK indexes + selected comments. See CONVENTIONS.md
and SCHEMA-MAP.md.
Soft-deletable: none in this module.
IMMUTABLE (created_at only, no updated_at): webhook_deliveries, email_log,
sms_log — these are append-only delivery/attempt records.

modules.name: audit
modules.description:
audit log, change history, access log, consent, compliance.
Compliance/governance module. Almost everything here is APPEND-ONLY: rows are
written once and never mutated, so immutable tables carry only created_at (or
occurred_at for event-shaped records) — NO updated_at, NO deleted_at. The few
genuinely mutable, lifecycle-bearing tables (data_exports, data_subject_requests,
retention_policies, legal_holds) keep updated_at because their status/fields
change over time.
FK targets (lower-or-equal modules only): tenants(id), users(id).
audit_log uses a POLYMORPHIC entity reference (entity_schema/entity_table/entity_id)
with NO real FK — by design: audited rows live in any of the 14 schemas and may be
hard-deleted, so a hard FK is impossible and intentionally absent.
See CONVENTIONS.md and SCHEMA-MAP.md.

modules.name: ops
modules.description:
feature flags, settings, jobs, integrations, files, imports.
Operational / platform-internal module. Mostly tenant-scoped config and
run records. Several tables here are IMMUTABLE (job_runs, integration_syncs,
import_errors, system_health_checks) and carry only created_at/occurred_at.
FK targets used: tenants(id), users(id), api_keys(id).
See CONVENTIONS.md and SCHEMA-MAP.md.

tables.name: tenants
tables.description:
tenants — the platform's customer organizations. NOT tenant-scoped (it IS
the tenant). default_currency_code / default_locale are wired to geo via
ALTERs at the end of 02_geo.sql (geo loads after identity).

columns.name: default_currency_code
columns.comment: ISO-4217 default currency; FK to currencies added in 02_geo.sql.

tables.comment: Customer organizations on the platform; the root of multi-tenancy. Every tenant-scoped row hangs off a tenant_id.

tables.name: users
tables.description:
users — end users and staff within a tenant. Emails are citext (case-
insensitive) and unique per tenant, not globally.

columns.name: is_staff
columns.comment: True for internal/admin operators of the tenant, as opposed to customer end-users.

tables.comment: End users and staff belonging to a tenant. Email is unique per tenant, not globally.

tables.name: roles
tables.description: RBAC: roles (per-tenant) + global permission catalog + junctions.
tables.comment: Per-tenant RBAC roles. is_system marks built-in roles that cannot be deleted.

tables.name: permissions
tables.comment: Global catalog of permission codes (e.g. orders.refund). Shared across all tenants.

tables.name: user_roles
tables.comment: Assignment of roles to users. granted_by_user_id records who made the grant.

tables.name: teams
tables.description: teams — hierarchical sub-org groupings.

tables.name: api_keys
tables.description: Credentials & auth artifacts.
tables.comment: Programmatic API credentials for a tenant. Only the hash and a short prefix are stored.

tables.name: sessions
tables.comment: Authenticated browser/app sessions. revoked_at non-null means force-logged-out.

tables.name: invitations
tables.comment: Pending invitations to join a tenant; consumed when status becomes accepted.

tables.name: login_attempts
tables.comment: Audit of authentication attempts, successful and failed, for security analytics.

tables.name: countries
tables.comment: ISO-3166 country reference. Global, shared by all tenants.

tables.name: currencies
tables.description: currencies: PK is id (per convention) but the FK target used everywhere is `code`.

columns.name: minor_unit
columns.comment: Number of decimal places (2 for USD, 0 for JPY).

tables.comment: ISO-4217 currencies. The code column (e.g. USD) is the FK target used by all monetary tables.

tables.name: exchange_rates
tables.comment: Daily FX rates between currency pairs, used to normalize multi-currency revenue.

tables.name: calendar_days

columns.name: calendar_date
columns.comment: The day.

columns.name: year_num
columns.comment: Calendar year.

columns.name: quarter_num
columns.comment: Calendar quarter, 1-4.

columns.name: month_num
columns.comment: Calendar month, 1-12.

columns.name: month_name
columns.comment: English month name, e.g. 'November'.

columns.name: month_label
columns.comment: Year and month as 'YYYY-MM'.

columns.name: day_of_month
columns.comment: Day of the month, 1-31.

columns.name: day_of_year
columns.comment: Day of the year, 1-366.

columns.name: iso_year
columns.comment: ISO 8601 week-numbering year (differs from year_num around New Year).

columns.name: iso_week
columns.comment: ISO 8601 week number, 1-53.

columns.name: iso_day_of_week
columns.comment: ISO day of the week: 1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday.

columns.name: day_name
columns.comment: English day name, e.g. 'Monday'.

columns.name: is_weekend
columns.comment: Saturday or Sunday.

columns.name: week_start
columns.comment: Monday of the ISO week.

columns.name: month_start
columns.comment: First day of the month.

columns.name: quarter_start
columns.comment: First day of the quarter.

tables.comment: Calendar dimension: one row per day from 2023-01-01 to 2026-12-31 with week, month and quarter attributes. Join to it to build complete time series (days, weeks or months without activity still appear).

tables.name: addresses
tables.description: addresses: tenant-scoped; optional owner user. One default per user via partial unique.
tables.comment: Postal addresses owned by a tenant and optionally a user. At most one default address per user.

tables.name: brands
tables.description: brands — manufacturer/brand records products belong to.
tables.comment: Manufacturer/brand records that products are grouped under.

tables.name: categories
tables.description:
categories — hierarchical product taxonomy. parent_id is a self-FK; the
transitive closure is materialized separately in category_closure.

checks.name: categories_not_self_parent_ck
checks.expr: parent_id IS NULL OR parent_id <> id

tables.comment: Hierarchical product taxonomy; parent_id is a self-reference to the parent category.

tables.name: category_closure
tables.description:
category_closure — ancestor/descendant pairs with depth, so subtree queries
("everything under Electronics") are a single join. depth 0 = self-row.

columns.name: depth
columns.comment: Number of edges between ancestor and descendant; 0 is the self-row.

tables.comment: Transitive closure of the category tree (ancestor, descendant, depth) for fast subtree queries.

tables.name: products
tables.description: products — the product master. public_id is the opaque external identifier.
tables.comment: Product master records; public_id is the opaque external identifier exposed via API/URL.

tables.name: product_variants
tables.description:
product_variants — the actual sellable SKUs under a product. sku is unique
per tenant. price_amount is a list/reference price; authoritative prices live
in the pricing module.

columns.name: is_default
columns.comment: Exactly one variant per product may be the default (enforced by a partial unique index).

checks.name: product_variants_price_currency_ck
checks.expr: price_amount IS NULL OR currency_code IS NOT NULL

tables.comment: Sellable SKUs of a product; sku is unique per tenant. Reference price only — authoritative pricing lives in the pricing schema.

tables.name: product_categories
tables.description:
product_categories — junction products×categories (a product can sit in many
categories beyond its primary one).

tables.name: attributes
tables.description:
attributes — definitions of product/variant attributes (e.g. Color, Size).
kind drives how attribute_values are interpreted.

columns.name: is_variant_defining
columns.comment: True when this attribute differentiates variants (Color, Size) rather than being descriptive.

tables.comment: Definitions of product/variant attributes (e.g. Color, Size); kind drives value interpretation.

tables.name: attribute_values
tables.description: attribute_values — allowed values for enum-kind attributes.
tables.comment: Allowed values for enum-kind attributes.

tables.name: variant_attribute_values
tables.description:
variant_attribute_values — junction variants×attribute_values, defining the
attribute combination that makes a variant unique (Color=Red, Size=L).
tables.comment: Junction binding a variant to its attribute/value pairs (the combination that makes it unique).

tables.name: product_media
tables.description:
product_media — images, video, and other media attached to products and
optionally a specific variant. kind is the media classification.
tables.comment: Images, video, and documents attached to a product and optionally a specific variant.

tables.name: collections
tables.description: collections — merchandising groupings (e.g. "Summer Sale", "New Arrivals").

checks.name: collections_window_ck
checks.expr: ends_at IS NULL OR starts_at IS NULL OR ends_at > starts_at

tables.comment: Merchandising groupings of products; may be manual or rule-driven (is_automated).

tables.name: collection_products
tables.description: collection_products — junction collections×products.

tables.name: tags
tables.description: tags — free-form labels applied to products.

tables.name: product_tags
tables.description: product_tags — junction products×tags.

tables.name: product_reviews
tables.description:
product_reviews — customer reviews of products. rating is 1-5 stars. user_id
is the reviewing users row; nullable for anonymized/imported reviews.

columns.name: is_verified_purchase
columns.comment: True when the reviewer is known to have purchased the product.

tables.comment: Customer reviews of products, rated 1-5 stars; one review per user per product.

tables.name: review_votes
tables.description: review_votes — helpfulness votes cast by users on a review.

tables.name: product_relations
tables.description:
product_relations — directional cross-sell / upsell / related pairs between
two products. relation_kind classifies the link.
tables.comment: Directional cross-sell/upsell/related links between two products.

tables.name: product_bundles
tables.description: product_bundles — header for a bundle/kit sold as a single offering.
tables.comment: Header for a bundle/kit sold as a single offering, composed of variant components.

tables.name: bundle_items
tables.description: bundle_items — the component variants (and quantities) that make up a bundle.
tables.comment: Component variants and quantities that make up a product bundle.

tables.name: price_lists
tables.description:
price_lists — named price books, each scoped to a single currency. A tenant
typically keeps one "default" list per currency plus contract/region books.

checks.name: price_lists_window_ck
checks.expr: ends_at IS NULL OR starts_at IS NULL OR ends_at > starts_at

tables.comment: Named price books, each scoped to one currency; a tenant keeps a default list per currency plus contract/regional books.

tables.name: prices
tables.description:
prices — a variant's price within a price_list, with a validity window. The
EXCLUDE constraint forbids two overlapping live windows for the same
(price_list, variant), so a variant never has an ambiguous price at a point
in time. valid_from/valid_to are materialized into a tstzrange for the gist.

columns.name: compare_at_amount
columns.comment: Optional strike-through / "was" price shown next to the effective amount.

checks.name: prices_window_ck
checks.expr: valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > valid_from

rules.name: prices_no_overlap
rules.description: Was EXCLUDE USING gist: for equal key, the half-open windows [valid_from, valid_to) must not overlap (NULL valid_to = open-ended).

tables.comment: A variant's price within a price list over a validity window; an exclusion constraint forbids overlapping windows for the same list/variant/min_quantity.

tables.name: discounts
tables.description:
discounts — reusable discount definitions (the "what"); coupons and
promotions point at these for the actual reduction. kind drives how value is
interpreted (percentage of subtotal, fixed amount off, free shipping, BOGO).

columns.name: discount_value
columns.comment: Percentage (0-100) when kind=percentage, else a fixed monetary amount in currency_code.

checks.name: discounts_fixed_currency_ck
checks.expr: kind <> 'fixed_amount' OR currency_code IS NOT NULL

tables.comment: Reusable discount definitions; coupons, price_rules and promotions point at these for the actual reduction.

tables.name: coupons
tables.description:
coupons — redeemable codes that grant a discount. code is unique per tenant.
usage_limit caps total redemptions; per_customer_limit caps per user.

columns.name: times_redeemed
columns.comment: Denormalized running count of redemptions, capped by usage_limit.

checks.name: coupons_window_ck
checks.expr: expires_at IS NULL OR starts_at IS NULL OR expires_at > starts_at

tables.comment: Redeemable codes granting a discount; code is unique per tenant and usage is capped by usage_limit / per_customer_limit.

tables.name: coupon_redemptions
tables.description:
coupon_redemptions — immutable record of each coupon use. References the
redeeming user (identity, lower-numbered). The redeemed order lives in sales
(module 06, higher-numbered): order_id is carried as a plain bigint and its
FK to orders(id) is added by 06_sales.sql via trailing ALTER, to keep
pricing free of any forward dependency. discount_amount is what was applied.
tables.comment: Immutable record of each coupon use; order_id references orders but its FK is added in 06_sales.sql to avoid a forward dependency.

tables.name: tax_categories
tables.description:
tax_categories — product tax classes (e.g. standard goods, digital, food,
exempt). Variants/products are mapped to one of these to find their rate.

tables.name: tax_zones
tables.description:
tax_zones — geographic regions for tax purposes. A zone is defined at the
granularity of a country, optionally narrowed to a region, optionally to a
specific postal zone. All three geo refs are nullable and SET NULL on delete.
tables.comment: Geographic tax regions defined at country, region or postal-zone granularity.

tables.name: tax_rates
tables.description:
tax_rates — the effective rate for a (tax_category, tax_zone) pair, with an
optional validity window so rate changes are auditable over time.

columns.name: rate
columns.comment: Fractional rate in [0,1]; e.g. 0.20000 for 20% VAT.

columns.name: is_inclusive
columns.comment: True when displayed prices already include this tax (tax-inclusive pricing).

checks.name: tax_rates_window_ck
checks.expr: valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > valid_from

tables.comment: Effective tax rate for a (tax_category, tax_zone) pair, with an optional validity window so rate changes stay auditable.

tables.name: price_rules
tables.description:
price_rules — conditional pricing rule headers (e.g. "10% off when cart has
3+ items from brand X"). Conditions live in price_rule_conditions. The reward
references a discount definition. priority orders evaluation; lower = first.

checks.name: price_rules_window_ck
checks.expr: ends_at IS NULL OR starts_at IS NULL OR ends_at > starts_at

tables.name: promotions
tables.description:
promotions — campaign-linked promo headers. STANDALONE on purpose: marketing
(module 10) FKs to promotions(id); we do NOT reference marketing. A
promotion grants a discount over a validity window, optionally gated by a
coupon code. campaign_code is a free-text correlation handle to a marketing
campaign, not an FK (marketing is higher-numbered).

columns.name: campaign_code
columns.comment: Free-text correlation handle to a marketing campaign; not an FK since marketing is a higher-numbered module.

checks.name: promotions_window_ck
checks.expr: ends_at IS NULL OR starts_at IS NULL OR ends_at > starts_at

tables.comment: Campaign-linked promotions; standalone by design so campaigns can reference promotions, never the reverse.

tables.name: promotion_products
tables.comment: Junction restricting a promotion to specific products.

tables.name: warehouses
tables.description:
warehouses — physical fulfillment sites. Each is anchored to a postal
address in geo. is_default marks the tenant's primary warehouse.
tables.comment: Physical fulfillment sites for a tenant, each anchored to a postal address; one is flagged as the default.

tables.name: stock_locations
tables.description:
stock_locations — bins/zones/aisles within a warehouse. The physical place
an item actually sits; stock is counted per location, not per warehouse.
tables.comment: Bins, shelves and zones inside a warehouse. Stock is counted at this granularity, not at the warehouse level.

tables.name: suppliers
tables.description: suppliers — vendors that goods are purchased from.
tables.comment: Vendors that goods are purchased from on purchase orders.

tables.name: supplier_products
tables.description:
supplier_products — a supplier's catalog mapping: their SKU + cost for one
of our variants. is_preferred picks the default source per variant.
tables.comment: Per-supplier sourcing of a variant: their SKU and unit cost; is_preferred marks the default source.

tables.name: stock_items
tables.description:
stock_items — the on-hand quantity of one variant in one location. This is
the live balance; stock_movements is the immutable history that produces it.
One row per (variant, location).

columns.name: reserved_quantity
columns.comment: Portion of quantity earmarked by open reservations and not available to sell.

columns.name: reorder_point
columns.comment: Replenishment trigger: at or below this on-hand level the variant is flagged for reorder.

indexes.name: stock_items_low_stock_idx
indexes.where: reorder_point IS NOT NULL AND quantity <= reorder_point

tables.comment: Live on-hand quantity of a variant in a single location; one row per (variant, location). The movements ledger is its history.

tables.name: stock_movements
tables.description:
stock_movements — IMMUTABLE append-only ledger of every quantity change.
quantity is SIGNED (positive = stock in, negative = stock out); summing the
ledger for a (variant, location) reproduces stock_items.quantity. No
updated_at: ledger rows are never mutated, only appended. reference_type /
reference_id loosely point at the source document (PO, order, adjustment).

columns.name: kind
columns.note: FK to lots added via ALTER below (lots is defined later in this file)

columns.name: reference_id
columns.comment: Loose pointer to the source document (PO line, order, adjustment) identified by reference_type; not a foreign key.

tables.comment: Immutable append-only ledger of inventory quantity changes; quantity is signed (in positive, out negative) and the running sum reproduces stock_items.

tables.name: stock_reservations
tables.description:
stock_reservations — soft holds that earmark on-hand stock for an order so
it isn't double-sold before fulfillment. order_id intentionally has NO FK:
orders lives in module 06 (higher-numbered) and the contract forbids
forward FKs; it is carried as a plain bigint reference. released_at non-null
means the hold was released (order shipped or cancelled).
tables.comment: Soft holds that earmark stock for an order so it is not double-sold; order_id references orders by id but has no FK (forward module).

tables.name: purchase_orders
tables.description:
purchase_orders — replenishment orders sent to a supplier, delivered to a
warehouse. public_id is the opaque external identifier. expected_total is a
denormalized convenience; the authoritative sum is over purchase_order_lines.

columns.name: expected_total
columns.comment: Denormalized order total; the authoritative figure is the sum over purchase_order_lines.

tables.comment: Replenishment orders sent to a supplier and delivered to a warehouse; public_id is the opaque external identifier.

tables.name: purchase_order_lines
tables.description:
purchase_order_lines — the variants and quantities on a PO, with the agreed
unit cost. quantity_received accrues as goods arrive against inbound_receipts.
tables.comment: Line items on a purchase order: variant, quantity and agreed unit cost, with received quantity accruing as goods arrive.

tables.name: lots
tables.description: lots — batch/lot tracking for a variant (manufacturing batch, expiry).

checks.name: lots_expiry_after_mfg_ck
checks.expr: expires_at IS NULL OR manufactured_at IS NULL OR expires_at >= manufactured_at

tables.comment: Batch/lot tracking for a variant, carrying manufacture and expiry dates for FEFO picking and recalls.

tables.name: serial_numbers
tables.description:
serial_numbers — individually tracked units (one row per physical unit),
optionally grouped under a lot and located in a stock location.

tables.name: inbound_receipts
tables.description: inbound_receipts — goods-receipt headers recording a delivery against a PO.
tables.comment: Goods-receipt headers recording a physical delivery into a warehouse, usually against a purchase order.

tables.name: receipt_lines
tables.description:
receipt_lines — the quantities of each variant actually received on a
receipt, put away into a specific location (and optionally a lot).

tables.name: stock_adjustments
tables.description:
stock_adjustments — manual corrections to on-hand quantity (cycle counts,
shrinkage, damage) with a required reason. quantity_delta is signed.
tables.comment: Manual corrections to on-hand stock (cycle counts, shrinkage, damage); quantity_delta is signed and a reason is required.

tables.name: carts
tables.description:
carts — shopping carts. May belong to a logged-in user or be anonymous
(user_id nullable). Converts to an order; see status cart_status.
tables.comment: Shopping carts, anonymous (user_id null) or owned. Converts to an order; abandoned carts feed recovery campaigns.

tables.name: orders
tables.description:
orders — the central order fact table. public_id is the opaque id surfaced
to customers. billing_address_id / shipping_address_id both -> addresses.
Totals are denormalized money; subtotal + tax + shipping - discount = grand.

columns.name: order_number
columns.comment: Human-facing sequential order number, unique per tenant (distinct from the opaque public_id).

columns.name: grand_total
columns.comment: Final amount charged: subtotal - discount_total + tax_total + shipping_total.

tables.comment: Central order fact table. public_id is the opaque id shown to customers; totals are denormalized money on the row.

tables.name: order_items

columns.name: quantity_fulfilled
columns.comment: Running count of units already dispatched across fulfillments; never exceeds quantity.

tables.comment: Line items of an order; sku and name are snapshotted at purchase time so historical orders survive catalog changes.

tables.name: order_status_history
tables.description:
order_status_history — append-only audit of order status transitions.
IMMUTABLE: created_at only, no updated_at, never soft-deleted.
tables.comment: Append-only audit of order status transitions; immutable (no updated_at).

tables.name: order_discounts
tables.description:
order_discounts — discounts/coupons applied to an order. references the
pricing module's discount/coupon definitions; either may be null (a manual
discount carries neither).
tables.comment: Discounts and coupon redemptions applied to an order; discount_id/coupon_id reference the pricing module.

tables.name: fulfillments
tables.description:
fulfillments — a shipment-able grouping of order items dispatched from a
warehouse. status fulfillment_status; FK warehouses.
tables.comment: A batch of order items dispatched together from one warehouse; tracks pick/pack/ship lifecycle.

tables.name: shipments
tables.description: shipments — carrier shipments per fulfillment, plus per-event tracking.
tables.comment: Carrier shipment for a fulfillment, with tracking number and delivery timestamps.

tables.name: shipment_tracking
tables.description:
shipment_tracking — append-only stream of carrier tracking events.
IMMUTABLE: occurred_at only, no updated_at.

tables.name: order_returns
tables.description:
returns — RMA headers. status return_status. return_items reference
the original order_items being returned.
tables.comment: Return merchandise authorization (RMA) header; status walks requested -> approved -> received -> refunded.

columns.name: restock
columns.comment: Whether the returned units should be added back to sellable inventory.

tables.name: gift_cards
tables.description:
gift_cards — stored-value instruments. code is unique per tenant.
gift_card_transactions is the append-only debit/credit ledger.
tables.comment: Stored-value gift cards; code is unique per tenant and balance decreases as it is redeemed against orders.

tables.name: gift_card_transactions
tables.description:
gift_card_transactions — immutable ledger of balance changes. Positive
amount = credit (issuance/top-up), negative = debit (redemption).
IMMUTABLE: created_at only, no updated_at.
tables.comment: Immutable ledger of gift-card balance changes; positive amount credits, negative debits.

tables.name: order_notes
tables.description:
order_notes — internal staff notes attached to an order (not the customer
note that lives on the order row itself).

tables.name: draft_orders
tables.description:
draft_orders — quotes / merchant-created draft orders, optionally converted
into a real order. payload holds the in-progress line items as schemaless json.
tables.comment: Merchant-created quotes/draft orders, optionally converted into a real order.

tables.name: billing_profiles
tables.description:
billing_profiles — the customer's billing entity for a tenant: legal name,
tax id, billing email, default payment method. One-or-more per tenant (e.g.
separate entities per region). Soft-deletable.

columns.name: net_terms_days
columns.comment: Payment terms in days (Net-0/Net-30/Net-60) before an invoice is past due.

tables.comment: Customer billing entity per tenant: legal name, tax id, billing email, net payment terms. One marked is_default per tenant.

tables.name: payment_methods
tables.description:
payment_methods — stored instruments (card, bank, paypal, wallet, ...).
Only a gateway token + last4/brand are kept, never raw PANs.

rules.name: payment_methods_one_default_idx
rules.where: is_default AND user_id IS NOT NULL

tables.comment: Stored payment instruments. Only a gateway token plus brand/last4 are kept; raw card numbers are never stored.

tables.name: payments
tables.description:
payments — a money-in capture against an order and/or an invoice. amount is
the gross captured; amount_refunded tracks cumulative refunds for quick
partial-refund checks.

columns.name: payment_method_id
columns.note: FK added via trailing ALTER (invoices defined later in this file)

columns.name: amount_refunded
columns.comment: Running total of amounts refunded against this payment; must never exceed amount.

tables.comment: Money-in captures against an order and/or invoice. amount_refunded tracks cumulative refunds for partial-refund accounting.

tables.name: payment_attempts
tables.description:
payment_attempts — each individual gateway round-trip for a payment. A
payment may need several attempts (retry on soft decline) before it captures.
tables.comment: Each gateway round-trip for a payment; a payment may need several attempts before it captures.

tables.name: payment_refunds
tables.description: payment_refunds — money-out reversing all or part of a captured payment.
tables.comment: Refunds reversing all or part of a captured payment, tracked through the refund_status lifecycle.

tables.name: invoices
tables.description:
invoices — billing documents (one-off or subscription). public_id is the
opaque external identifier. amount_due drives dunning; amount_paid +
amount_due reconcile against total.

columns.name: invoice_number
columns.note: FK added via trailing ALTER (subscriptions defined later in this file)

columns.name: amount_due
columns.comment: Outstanding balance still owed; reaches 0 when the invoice is fully paid.

tables.comment: Billing documents (one-off or subscription). amount_due drives dunning; public_id is the opaque external identifier.

tables.name: invoice_lines
tables.description:
invoice_lines — line items on an invoice. line_total = unit_price * quantity
(pre-tax); tax_amount is the line's tax contribution.

columns.name: description
columns.note: FK added via trailing ALTER (subscription_items defined later in this file)

checks.name: invoice_lines_period_chk
checks.expr: period_end IS NULL OR period_start IS NULL OR period_end > period_start

tables.comment: Line items on an invoice; optionally tied to a subscription_item, with the service period it covers.

tables.name: credit_notes
tables.description:
credit_notes — credit memos issued against an invoice (returns, goodwill,
corrections). May or may not be tied to a specific invoice.
tables.comment: Credit memos issued against invoices for returns, goodwill, or corrections.

tables.name: payouts
tables.description:
payouts — settlement of collected funds out to the tenant (Stripe-Connect-
style). gross = sum of settled payments; fees deducted; net = paid out.
tables.comment: Settlements of collected funds out to the tenant; net = gross minus fees.

tables.name: payout_items
tables.description:
payout_items — the individual payments settled within a payout. A payment
appears in at most one payout.
tables.comment: The individual payments settled within a payout; each payment appears in at most one payout.

tables.name: ledger_accounts
tables.description:
ledger_accounts — the tenant's chart of accounts for the double-entry
ledger. type is the accounting class (asset/liability/revenue/...).

tables.name: ledger_entries
tables.description:
ledger_entries — IMMUTABLE append-only double-entry lines. Each row is one
debit or credit against one account; balanced postings share a entry_group
(the journal entry). No updated_at: ledgers are never mutated, only reversed
by a compensating entry.

columns.name: entry_group
columns.comment: Groups the debit/credit rows of a single balanced journal entry (their amounts must net to zero).

tables.comment: Immutable append-only double-entry ledger lines. Postings sharing an entry_group form one balanced journal entry.

tables.name: plans
tables.description:
plans — subscription products. code is the stable external key, unique per
tenant. default_interval is the billing cadence; trial_period_days seeds the
trialing window.
tables.comment: Subscription products. code is the stable per-tenant key; default_interval sets the billing cadence.

tables.name: plan_features
tables.description:
plan_features — feature limits/entitlements per plan (e.g. seats=10,
api_calls=100000). limit_value NULL means unlimited.

columns.name: limit_value
columns.comment: Quota for the feature (e.g. seats, api_calls); NULL means unlimited.

tables.comment: Feature entitlements/limits per plan; limit_value NULL means unlimited.

tables.name: plan_prices
tables.description:
plan_prices — price points for a plan, one per currency × interval. A plan
can be billed monthly in USD, yearly in EUR, etc.
tables.comment: Price points for a plan, one per currency and billing interval.

tables.name: subscriptions
tables.description:
subscriptions — a user's recurring commitment to a plan. public_id is the
opaque external id. current_period_* drive the next invoice; cancel_at_period_end
defers cancellation to the period boundary.

columns.name: cancel_at_period_end
columns.comment: When true the subscription cancels at current_period_end rather than immediately.

checks.name: subscriptions_period_chk
checks.expr: current_period_end IS NULL OR current_period_start IS NULL OR current_period_end > current_period_start

tables.comment: A user's recurring commitment to a plan. current_period_* bound the next invoice; cancel_at_period_end defers cancellation.

tables.name: subscription_items
tables.description:
subscription_items — line items / add-ons of a subscription, each priced via
a plan_price. unit_amount snapshots the price at subscription time.
tables.comment: Line items / add-ons of a subscription; unit_amount snapshots the price at the time of subscription.

tables.name: usage_records
tables.description:
usage_records — metered usage events feeding consumption billing. Each row
is a quantity reported for a metered subscription_item in a period.
tables.comment: Metered usage reported for a subscription_item, aggregated into consumption-based invoice lines.

tables.name: dunning_attempts
tables.description:
dunning_attempts — the retry sequence chasing payment on a past-due invoice.
next_attempt_at schedules the following retry.
tables.comment: Retry sequence chasing payment on a past-due invoice; next_attempt_at schedules the following retry.

tables.name: tax_registrations
tables.description:
tax_registrations — the tenant's tax IDs per jurisdiction (VAT, GST, sales
tax). Drives whether/how tax is charged in a region.

columns.name: registration_number
columns.comment: The official tax/VAT registration number issued by the jurisdiction.

checks.name: tax_registrations_validity_chk
checks.expr: valid_until IS NULL OR valid_from IS NULL OR valid_until > valid_from

tables.comment: Tenant tax IDs per jurisdiction (VAT/GST/sales tax) governing how tax is charged in a region.

tables.name: wallets
tables.description:
wallets — stored-credit balances per user (prepaid credit, refunds-to-credit,
promo balance). balance is always in the wallet's currency.
tables.comment: Stored-credit balances per user and currency (prepaid credit, refunds-to-credit, promo balance).

tables.name: accounts
tables.description:
accounts — the tenant's B2B customer companies. Owner is an internal rep
(users). Self-referencing parent links live in account_relationships.

columns.name: owner_user_id
columns.comment: Internal sales rep (users) who owns the account relationship.

tables.comment: The tenant's own B2B customer companies. Tenant-scoped; distinct from tenants (the platform's customers).

tables.name: contacts
tables.description:
contacts — people who work at an account. Primary email is denormalized for
convenience; the full set lives in contact_emails.
tables.comment: People who work at a CRM account. primary_email is denormalized; the full set lives in contact_emails.

tables.name: contact_emails
tables.description: contact_emails — multiple email addresses per contact (work, personal, ...).
tables.comment: All email addresses for a contact; at most one flagged is_primary per contact.

tables.name: leads
tables.description:
leads — unqualified inbound interest, before becoming an account/contact.
Converts forward into account_id / contact_id once qualified.

columns.name: score
columns.comment: Lead score (0+); higher means more sales-ready.

tables.comment: Unqualified inbound interest before it becomes an account/contact; converts forward once qualified.

tables.name: pipelines
tables.description: pipelines — named sales pipelines per tenant. Stages are in opportunity_stages.
tables.comment: Named sales pipelines per tenant; at most one is the default. Stages live in opportunity_stages.

tables.name: opportunity_stages
tables.description:
opportunity_stages — ordered LOOKUP of stages within a pipeline. position
defines the funnel order; win_probability drives weighted forecasts.

columns.name: win_probability
columns.comment: Default close probability for opportunities in this stage, 0..1.

tables.comment: Ordered lookup of stages within a pipeline. position sets funnel order; win_probability drives weighted forecasts.

tables.name: opportunities
tables.description:
opportunities — deals in flight. Lives in a pipeline at a stage, tied to an
account. amount is the expected contract value in currency_code.
tables.comment: Deals in flight: an account being worked through a pipeline stage with an expected amount.

tables.name: deals
tables.description:
deals — closed-won contracts realized from an opportunity. Holds the booked
contract value and term.

checks.name: deals_term_valid
checks.expr: ends_at IS NULL OR starts_at IS NULL OR ends_at > starts_at

tables.comment: Closed-won contracts realized from an opportunity, holding the booked contract value and term.

tables.name: deal_line_items
tables.description: deal_line_items — products sold on a deal, priced per unit in the deal currency.
tables.comment: Products sold on a deal, priced per unit in the deal currency.

tables.name: activities
tables.description:
activities — logged interactions (calls/emails/meetings/notes/tasks). The
target is polymorphic-ish: any of account/contact/opportunity may be set.

checks.name: activities_has_target
checks.expr: account_id IS NOT NULL OR contact_id IS NOT NULL OR opportunity_id IS NOT NULL

tables.comment: Logged interactions (calls, emails, meetings) against an account, contact, or opportunity.

tables.name: crm_notes
tables.description: crm_notes — free-text notes attached to a CRM entity (polymorphic target).

checks.name: crm_notes_has_target
checks.expr: account_id IS NOT NULL OR contact_id IS NOT NULL OR opportunity_id IS NOT NULL

tables.name: tasks
tables.description: tasks — follow-up to-dos for reps, optionally linked to a CRM entity.
tables.comment: Follow-up to-dos assigned to reps, optionally linked to a CRM entity.

tables.name: account_relationships
tables.description:
account_relationships — parent/subsidiary and other links between accounts.
child_account_id is the dependent; parent_account_id the controlling entity.
tables.comment: Parent/subsidiary and other directed links between accounts within a tenant.

tables.name: contact_lists
tables.description: contact_lists — static, manually-curated lists of contacts.

tables.name: contact_list_members
tables.description: contact_list_members — junction of contacts into static lists.

tables.name: support_agents
tables.description:
support_agents — staff who work tickets. One record per agent user (a thin
support-specific extension of users carrying availability/load).
tables.comment: Support staff who handle tickets; a support-specific extension of an users record carrying availability and load limits.

tables.name: agent_groups
tables.description: agent_groups — named teams of agents for routing/assignment.
tables.comment: Named groups of agents used for ticket routing and assignment.

tables.name: sla_policies
tables.description:
sla_policies — lookup of response/resolution targets (minutes) applied to
tickets, typically by priority.

columns.name: business_hours_only
columns.comment: When true, SLA timers pause outside the tenant business calendar rather than running 24/7.

tables.comment: Lookup of service-level targets (first-response and resolution minutes), usually keyed by ticket priority.

tables.name: support_tags
tables.description: support_tags — tag catalog for categorizing tickets.

tables.name: knowledge_categories
tables.description: Knowledge base: hierarchical categories + articles + per-article feedback.

tables.name: knowledge_articles

columns.name: helpful_count
columns.comment: Denormalized count of positive article_feedback rows, kept for fast sorting.

tables.comment: Help-center articles published to customers; soft-deletable via deleted_at.

tables.name: macros
tables.description: macros — canned replies agents can insert into tickets. Soft-deletable.
tables.comment: Canned reply templates agents insert into ticket messages. Soft-deletable.

tables.name: tickets
tables.description:
tickets — the core support request. public_id is the opaque external id.
requester_user_id is the customer; assignee_agent_id is nullable (unassigned
queue) and SET NULL when the agent record is removed.

columns.name: first_response_at
columns.comment: Timestamp of the first public agent reply, used to measure SLA first-response compliance.

tables.comment: Core customer support request. requester_user_id is the customer; assignee_agent_id is the owning agent (null = unassigned queue).

tables.name: ticket_messages
tables.description:
ticket_messages — public replies (customer-visible) and private internal
notes (is_public = false). Author is an agent OR the requesting user.
tables.comment: Replies on a ticket: is_public=true are customer-visible, is_public=false are internal agent notes.

tables.name: ticket_events
tables.description:
ticket_events — IMMUTABLE append-only audit of ticket changes (status flips,
reassignment, priority bumps). occurred_at only; no updated_at.
tables.comment: Immutable append-only audit of ticket changes such as status transitions, reassignment, and priority changes.

tables.name: ticket_tags_map
tables.description: ticket_tags_map — junction tickets × support_tags.

tables.name: sla_breaches
tables.description: sla_breaches — recorded breach of an SLA target on a ticket.
tables.comment: Recorded SLA-target breaches on a ticket, with how many minutes the target was missed by.

tables.name: csat_responses
tables.description: csat_responses — customer satisfaction score (1-5) submitted per ticket.

columns.name: rated_agent_id
columns.comment: The agent the customer was rating, captured at submission in case the ticket is later reassigned.

tables.comment: Customer satisfaction rating (1-5) collected after a ticket is resolved; one response per ticket.

tables.name: email_templates
tables.description:
email_templates — reusable rendered email bodies referenced by campaigns and
per-recipient sends. Defined first so campaign_messages can FK it.
tables.comment: Reusable email subject/body templates used by campaigns and per-recipient sends.

tables.name: segments
tables.description:
segments — audience definitions. The actual selection logic lives in `rules`
(jsonb); segment_members materializes the current membership.

columns.name: is_dynamic
columns.comment: True if membership is recomputed from rules on a schedule; false for static lists.

tables.comment: Audience definitions; the selection logic lives in the rules jsonb and is materialized into segment_members.

tables.name: landing_pages
tables.description:
landing_pages — campaign destination pages. Referenced by campaigns and
utm_links, so defined ahead of them.

tables.name: campaigns
tables.description:
campaigns — marketing campaigns. May optionally target a segment, render via
an email_template, drive to a landing_page, and link a promotion.

checks.name: campaigns_window_chk
checks.expr: ended_at IS NULL OR started_at IS NULL OR ended_at > started_at

checks.name: campaigns_budget_currency_chk
checks.expr: budget IS NULL OR currency_code IS NOT NULL

tables.comment: Marketing campaigns; may target a segment, render via a template, drive to a landing page, and link a pricing promotion.

tables.name: campaign_messages
tables.description:
campaign_messages — one row per recipient send. send_status tracks the
delivery/engagement lifecycle (queued -> sent -> opened -> clicked ...).
tables.comment: One row per recipient send; send_status tracks the delivery and engagement lifecycle.

tables.name: ab_tests
tables.description: A/B testing: ab_tests -> ab_variants -> ab_assignments(user -> variant).

checks.name: ab_tests_window_chk
checks.expr: ended_at IS NULL OR started_at IS NULL OR ended_at > started_at

tables.comment: A/B test definitions; winner_variant_id records the chosen variant once the experiment completes.

rules.name: ab_tests_winner_variant_fk
rules.description: winner_variant_id, when set, is a variant of this same test (was a FOREIGN KEY; removed to break the ab_tests <-> ab_variants cycle).
rules.violations_sql: SELECT t.id FROM ab_tests t WHERE t.winner_variant_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ab_variants v WHERE v.id = t.winner_variant_id AND v.ab_test_id = t.id)

columns.name: traffic_weight
columns.comment: Fraction of eligible traffic routed to this variant; weights across a test should sum to ~1.

tables.name: ab_assignments
tables.comment: Sticky assignment of a user to one variant within an A/B test; converted_at records goal completion.

tables.name: attributions
tables.description:
attributions — touch attributions linking a marketing surface to a
conversion. order_id is a NULLABLE backward FK to orders (allowed): set
when the touch is credited with an order, null for non-purchase conversions.

columns.name: weight
columns.comment: Fractional credit for this touch under the attribution model (e.g. linear, last_touch).

checks.name: attributions_revenue_currency_chk
checks.expr: attributed_revenue IS NULL OR currency_code IS NOT NULL

tables.comment: Touch attributions crediting a campaign with a conversion; order_id is set for purchase conversions.

tables.name: referrals
tables.description:
referrals — referral codes owned by a referring user; referral_redemptions
record a new user redeeming a code.

checks.name: referrals_reward_currency_chk
checks.expr: reward_amount IS NULL OR currency_code IS NOT NULL

tables.comment: Referral codes owned by a referring user, with optional reward and redemption caps.

checks.name: referral_redemptions_reward_currency_chk
checks.expr: reward_amount IS NULL OR currency_code IS NOT NULL

tables.name: loyalty_programs
tables.description:
Loyalty: program defs -> per-user accounts (balance) -> immutable earn/burn
transaction ledger.

checks.name: loyalty_programs_window_chk
checks.expr: ends_at IS NULL OR starts_at IS NULL OR ends_at > starts_at

tables.name: loyalty_accounts
tables.comment: Per-user point balance within a loyalty program; points_balance is the current redeemable total.

tables.name: loyalty_transactions
tables.description: IMMUTABLE ledger: append-only earn/burn rows. created_at only, no updated_at.

columns.name: balance_after
columns.comment: Account points_balance immediately after this entry was applied.

tables.comment: Immutable earn/burn ledger of loyalty point movements; append-only, never updated.

tables.name: utm_links
tables.description:
utm_links — tracked short/long URLs with UTM params, optionally tied to a
campaign and/or landing_page.
tables.comment: Tracked links carrying UTM parameters, optionally tied to a campaign and landing page.

tables.name: web_sessions
tables.description:
web_sessions — analytics sessions, DISTINCT from sessions (which
are auth sessions). A web session groups a visitor's activity; user_id is
nullable because anonymous (pre-login) traffic still produces sessions.

columns.name: anonymous_id
columns.comment: Client-generated visitor identifier used to stitch sessions before the user authenticates.

checks.name: web_sessions_ended_after_started_ck
checks.expr: ended_at IS NULL OR ended_at >= started_at

tables.comment: Visitor analytics sessions, distinct from sessions (auth). Anonymous traffic still produces a session with a null user_id.

tables.name: events
tables.description:
events — THE big fact table (bench scale ~10M rows). Immutable: only
occurred_at/created_at, no updated_at/deleted_at. user_id and web_session_id
are nullable; user deletion sets user_id NULL rather than dropping events.

columns.name: web_session_id
columns.comment: Nullable link to the analytics web session this event occurred in; server-side events may have none.

tables.comment: The primary product analytics fact table (~10M rows at bench scale). Each row is one tracked event with a free-form event_name and schemaless jsonb properties.

tables.name: page_views
tables.description:
page_views — individual page hits within a web session. Immutable log:
viewed_at only, no updated_at.
tables.comment: Individual page hits within a web session, used for path and dwell-time analysis.

tables.name: device_profiles
tables.description:
device_profiles — browser/device fingerprints observed per tenant. A
profile may be linked to a user once they authenticate.
tables.comment: Browser/device fingerprints observed per tenant, optionally linked to a user once authenticated.

tables.name: feature_usage
tables.description:
feature_usage — per-user product-feature adoption counters. Aggregated
usage rolled up per (user, feature, day); immutable counter snapshot row.

columns.name: feature_key
columns.comment: Stable identifier of the product feature being measured (e.g. bulk_export, dashboard_share).

tables.comment: Per-user, per-day product feature adoption counters feeding engagement and stickiness metrics.

tables.name: experiments
tables.description:
experiments — product experiments (server-side / feature experiments,
distinct from ab_tests). status reuses experiment_status.

checks.name: experiments_window_ck
checks.expr: ends_at IS NULL OR starts_at IS NULL OR ends_at > starts_at

tables.comment: Server-side product experiments (feature experiments), distinct from ab_tests which are message-level tests.

tables.name: experiment_variants
tables.comment: Variants (arms) of an experiment; exactly one may be flagged is_control, with allocation_pct summing across arms.

tables.name: experiment_assignments
tables.comment: Records which variant a user (or anonymous visitor) was bucketed into for an experiment.

tables.name: funnels
tables.description: funnels — ordered conversion-funnel definitions and their steps.
tables.comment: Ordered conversion-funnel definitions evaluated over the events stream.

tables.name: cohorts
tables.description: cohorts — named user cohorts and their materialized membership.
tables.comment: Named user cohorts, dynamic (rule-based) or static, used for retention and segmentation analysis.

tables.name: metrics_daily
tables.description:
metrics_daily — pre-aggregated daily metric values per tenant. One row per
(tenant, metric_key, day). dimensions holds optional breakdown labels.

columns.name: dimensions
columns.comment: Optional breakdown labels (e.g. {"channel":"organic"}) when a metric is sliced; empty object for the headline total.

tables.comment: Pre-aggregated daily metric values per tenant; one row per (tenant, metric_key, day) for fast dashboard reads.

tables.name: kpi_snapshots
tables.description:
kpi_snapshots — periodic captures of headline KPIs (MRR, active users,
conversion rate, ...) for trend dashboards.
tables.comment: Periodic captures of headline KPIs (MRR, active users, conversion rate) with the prior-period value for trend deltas.

tables.name: notification_templates
tables.description:
notification_templates — reusable notification bodies, keyed per tenant and
channel. Referenced (nullably) by notifications that were rendered from a
template vs. composed ad hoc.
tables.comment: Reusable, per-tenant notification bodies keyed by code and channel; rendered into notifications and email/sms logs.

tables.name: notifications
tables.description:
notifications — per-user notifications with a delivery lifecycle. May be
rendered from a template or composed directly (template_id nullable).
tables.comment: Per-user notifications with a queued→sent→delivered→read lifecycle. template_id is null when composed ad hoc.

tables.name: notification_preferences
tables.description: notification_preferences — per-user opt-in matrix by channel and category.
tables.comment: Per-user opt-in matrix across channels and categories; an absent row means the tenant default applies.

tables.name: message_threads
tables.description:
message_threads — in-app conversation threads (e.g. between a customer and
the tenant's support/comms). Holds an optional owning user.
tables.comment: In-app conversation threads between a tenant and a user. last_message_at is denormalized for inbox sorting.

tables.name: thread_messages
tables.description:
thread_messages — individual messages within a thread. direction marks
whether the message is inbound (from the user) or outbound (from the tenant).

columns.name: direction
columns.comment: inbound = sent by the user toward the tenant; outbound = sent by the tenant toward the user.

tables.name: webhooks
tables.description:
webhooks — subscriber endpoints that receive event callbacks. secret_hash
is used to sign delivery payloads; only the hash is stored.

columns.name: secret_hash
columns.comment: Hash of the HMAC signing secret used to sign delivery payloads; the plaintext secret is shown once at creation.

tables.comment: Subscriber HTTP endpoints that receive signed event callbacks. Only the hash of the signing secret is stored.

tables.name: webhook_deliveries
tables.description:
webhook_deliveries — IMMUTABLE append-only log of each delivery attempt for
a webhook subscription, including the response code and retry attempt count.

columns.name: attempt
columns.comment: 1-based retry counter; multiple rows per logical event when a delivery is retried.

tables.comment: Append-only log of each webhook delivery attempt, including HTTP response_code and retry attempt number.

tables.name: email_log
tables.description:
email_log — IMMUTABLE record of each outbound email sent on behalf of a
tenant. recipient_email is stored denormalized (the user may be deleted or
the address may be off-platform).
tables.comment: Immutable record of every outbound email; recipient_email is denormalized since the user or address may be off-platform.

tables.name: sms_log
tables.description:
sms_log — IMMUTABLE record of each outbound SMS. (Intentionally uncommented
at table level — see CONVENTIONS.md on deliberate comment gaps.)

tables.name: push_tokens
tables.description:
push_tokens — device push-notification tokens registered per user. A token
is unique per tenant; (user, platform, device) identifies a device install.
tables.comment: Device push-notification tokens per user; deactivated rather than deleted when a device unregisters.

tables.name: unsubscribes
tables.description:
unsubscribes — suppression list of addresses/channels that must not receive
further messages. user_id is nullable (an address may unsubscribe without an
account); the address is stored denormalized for matching.
tables.comment: Suppression list of addresses/channels that must be excluded from further sends; user_id may be null for off-platform addresses.

tables.name: contact_channels
tables.description:
contact_channels — verified contact endpoints (email/phone) per user, with
a verification lifecycle. At most one primary channel of each kind per user.
tables.comment: Verified contact endpoints (email/phone) per user with a verification lifecycle; one primary per kind via a partial unique index.

tables.name: audit_log
tables.description:
audit_log — the central append-only audit trail. Every meaningful mutation
and security-relevant action lands here. The audited entity is referenced
polymorphically (schema + table + row id) because it can live anywhere in
the database and may later be deleted. Immutable: occurred_at only.

columns.name: actor_type
columns.comment: Principal kind that performed the action: user, api_key, service_account, or system.

columns.name: entity_id
columns.comment: Primary-key id of the audited row in entity_schema.entity_table; intentionally not a foreign key.

tables.comment: Central append-only audit trail of meaningful mutations and security actions. The audited row is referenced polymorphically via entity_schema/entity_table/entity_id (no FK).

tables.name: change_history
tables.description:
change_history — column-level before/after diffs for an audited row. Often
written alongside an audit_log entry but can stand alone. Immutable.
tables.comment: Column-level before/after JSON diffs for an audited row, usually linked to an audit_log entry.

tables.name: access_log
tables.description:
access_log — records reads of sensitive data (PII, financial, exports) for
compliance and breach forensics. Append-only, very high volume.
tables.comment: Append-only record of reads of sensitive/PII data, for compliance and breach forensics.

tables.name: data_exports
tables.description:
data_exports — GDPR / data-portability export jobs. Tracks request through
completion; the produced artifact lives in object storage (file_url).

tables.name: consent_records
tables.description:
consent_records — per-user consent grants/withdrawals for a named purpose
(marketing, analytics, terms, ...). Append-only consent history; the latest
row per (user, purpose) is the effective state. status consent_status.

columns.name: policy_version
columns.comment: Version of the privacy policy / terms the user consented to at the time.

tables.comment: Append-only per-user consent grants and withdrawals by purpose; the latest row per (user, purpose) is the effective consent state.

tables.name: compliance_events
tables.description:
compliance_events — flagged compliance incidents / policy violations needing
review (suspicious access, retention overrun, failed DSAR SLA, ...).

tables.name: data_subject_requests
tables.description:
data_subject_requests — DSAR / right-to-erasure / access / rectification
requests under GDPR/CCPA. Mutable lifecycle: status changes as the request
is processed, so this table keeps updated_at. FK-targetable key (id).

columns.name: request_type
columns.comment: Kind of DSAR: access, erasure, rectification, portability, or restriction.

checks.name: dsr_subject_present_chk
checks.expr: subject_user_id IS NOT NULL OR subject_email IS NOT NULL

tables.comment: GDPR/CCPA data-subject requests (access, erasure, rectification, portability) tracked through their processing lifecycle.

tables.name: retention_policies
tables.description:
retention_policies — per-entity data-retention rules driving automated
purges. Mutable config: rules are edited over time, so keeps updated_at.
FK-targetable key (id) — legal_holds reference the policy they suspend.
tables.comment: Per-entity data-retention rules (retention_days + action_on_expiry) driving automated purges.

tables.name: legal_holds
tables.description:
legal_holds — suspend deletion/retention for a subject or entity scope while
litigation/investigation is pending. Mutable: a hold is released over time.

checks.name: legal_holds_release_chk
checks.expr: released_at IS NULL OR released_at >= placed_at

tables.comment: Active legal/investigation holds that suspend retention-driven deletion for a subject or entity scope.

tables.name: audit_log_archive
tables.description:
audit_log_archive — cold copy of aged-out audit_log rows. Same shape as
audit_log, written once by the archival job and never mutated. Keeps the
original id as source_audit_log_id for provenance.
tables.comment: Cold archive of aged-out audit_log rows; same shape as audit_log, written once by the archival job. source_audit_log_id preserves the original id.

tables.name: feature_flags
tables.description: feature_flags — toggle/rollout definitions, keyed uniquely per tenant.

columns.name: default_value
columns.comment: Fallback value served when no rule or override matches; jsonb to support multivariate payloads, not just booleans.

tables.comment: Feature toggle and rollout definitions, addressed by a tenant-unique key. kind distinguishes boolean toggles from multivariate and percentage rollouts.

tables.name: feature_flag_rules
tables.comment: Ordered targeting rules for a flag; the first rule whose jsonb conditions match decides the served value.

tables.name: feature_flag_overrides
tables.comment: Explicit per-user or tenant-wide overrides that bypass rule evaluation for a flag.

tables.name: settings
tables.description: settings — typed key/value configuration store, scoped per tenant.

columns.name: value_type
columns.comment: Logical type hint for value (string/number/boolean/json/date); the column itself is always jsonb.

tables.comment: Typed key/value configuration per tenant. value_type tags how the jsonb value should be interpreted by the application.

tables.name: jobs
tables.description: jobs / job_runs — background job definitions and their (immutable) executions.
tables.comment: Background job definitions registered per tenant; job_runs records each execution.

tables.name: job_runs

checks.name: job_runs_finish_chk
checks.expr: finished_at IS NULL OR started_at IS NULL OR finished_at >= started_at

tables.comment: Immutable record of a single background job execution, including status, attempt number and timing.

tables.name: integrations
tables.description: integrations / integration_syncs — third-party connections and sync runs.
tables.comment: Third-party service connections for a tenant (e.g. ERP, shipping, accounting), with current status and config.

tables.name: integration_syncs

checks.name: integration_syncs_finish_chk
checks.expr: finished_at IS NULL OR started_at IS NULL OR finished_at >= started_at

tables.comment: Immutable record of a single data-sync run against an integration.

tables.name: files
tables.description:
files / file_versions — uploaded file metadata (blobs live in object storage)
plus an explicit version chain per file.
tables.comment: Metadata for files uploaded to object storage; the actual blob lives in storage_bucket/storage_key, not in the database.

tables.name: file_versions
tables.comment: Version chain for a file; is_current flags the active version (one per file, enforced by partial unique index).

tables.name: import_batches
tables.description:
import_batches / import_errors — bulk import runs and their (immutable)
per-row failures.

checks.name: import_batches_finish_chk
checks.expr: finished_at IS NULL OR started_at IS NULL OR finished_at >= started_at

tables.comment: Bulk data-import runs with row-level progress counters and a terminal status.

tables.name: import_errors
tables.comment: Immutable per-row failures captured during an import batch, with the offending raw row preserved as jsonb.

tables.name: scheduled_tasks
tables.description: scheduled_tasks — cron-expression driven recurring tasks.
tables.comment: Cron-expression driven recurring tasks; next_run_at is the precomputed next fire time used by the scheduler.

tables.name: system_health_checks
tables.description: system_health_checks — immutable periodic health probe results.

tables.name: rate_limits
tables.description: rate_limits — per-tenant / per-api-key quota windows.
tables.comment: Request quota windows scoped per tenant or per API key; an api_key-null row is the tenant-wide default for a scope.

tables.name: secrets_vault
tables.description:
secrets_vault — references/metadata for externally-stored secrets. NEVER
stores plaintext: only a pointer (provider + external ref) and metadata.

columns.name: external_ref
columns.comment: Opaque pointer into the external secret store (e.g. a Vault path or KMS key id); resolved at runtime, never the secret value itself.

tables.comment: References and metadata for secrets held in an external vault; never stores plaintext, only a provider pointer (external_ref).
